chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal, from Ula'a ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the most hated names to Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, are Harith, Malik, and Khalid.

key_terms.حَارِثٌ: Harith (a name meaning 'cultivator' or 'owner of crops')

ai.seo_question: What are the most hated names to Allah in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Harith, Malik, and Khalid as the most disliked names because their etymological meanings—'provider,' 'owner,' and 'eternal'—can imply independent divine attributes when attributed to creation. This critique is central to Shia theological emphasis on Tawhid, warning against subtle shirk by ensuring humans do not appropriate titles that belong exclusively to Allah. The ruling highlights the importance of linguistic precision in reflecting the humility of the created servant before the Sovereign Lord.
